summary: V3-05 candidate implements the À faire experience: full todo creation form (titre, assigné, bénéficiaires, échéance, rappel, note, PersistentTask raccourcis), completion mini-form (Fait par, valeur selon l'unité du groupe, bénéficiaires), free delete with confirmation, honest notification/calendar ports (isAvailable()=false, no-op), data-change signals ('todo' added to DataChangeType; balances.tsx widened to the shared type with no behavioral change), and a pure domain service planTodoCompletion that validates and produces exactly one ContributionEntry with the household's current unit plus the completed todo. Trusted verification passed (exit 0: typecheck, 196 tests green, Expo export, prebuild, native debug BUILD SUCCESSFUL); independent re-run of the two new suites (16 tests) green; no chrono, no premium/paywall/entitlement, no V2 warm design, no silent unit conversion, no data destruction, local-first SQLite todos with indexes, bounded writes (create=1, complete=2, delete=1) and bounded load reads (4, no N+1). MUST-FIX remains: the completion is not atomic. app/(tabs)/todos.tsx handleComplete executes the two coupled writes (todo status update + contribution creation) via Promise.all, which is not a transaction: an independent probe demonstrated that when the todo update fails, the contribution is still created (orphan entry), so a retry creates a second ContributionEntry (violating 'exactement une ContributionEntry atomique'), and the inverse failure (contribution create fails after todo update succeeds) silently loses the ledger entry because completed todos are filtered from the list. The test 'creating the contribution and updating the todo is atomic in the repos' only exercises the success path and asserts 'both succeed or both fail' without testing failure atomicity — a weak test. Backend frugal §7 requires coupled changes to use batch/transaction/atomic business operation. Decision: repair (coherent WIP baseline preserved).

Independent atomicity probe (temporary test, removed after run): with the todo deleted before Promise.all, todoRepo.update rejects while contribRepo.create succeeds — contributionsCreated=1 leaked despite the 'atomic' failure, proving Promise.all is not atomic and the existing test does not guard the failure path

findings.problem: MUST-FIX — the completion is not atomic. The two coupled writes (todo status update + ContributionEntry creation) are executed with Promise.all, which is not a transaction. Failure scenario A: if repos.todos.update rejects after repos.contributions.create resolved, an orphan ContributionEntry exists while the todo stays active; the user sees 'Impossible de terminer la tache' and a retry creates a SECOND ContributionEntry — violating the V3-05 acceptance 'exactement une ContributionEntry atomique'. Failure scenario B: if repos.contributions.create rejects after the todo update resolved, the todo is marked completed (and filtered out of the list) with no ledger entry — silent loss of the contribution. The test named 'creating the contribution and updating the todo is atomic in the repos' only exercises the success path and asserts 'both succeed or both fail' without ever simulating a failure — a weak test that does not guard the invariant. Backend frugal §7: 'Les changements couplés doivent employer batch/transaction/opération métier atomique.'
findings.evidence: todos.tsx lines 247-254: `await Promise.all([repos.todos.update(selectedTodo.id, {status:'completed', completedAt:...}), repos.contributions.create(result.contributionEntry)])`. Independent probe (temporary test, removed): deleting the todo before the Promise.all makes todoRepo.update throw while contribRepo.create still succeeds — console output 'todoUpdateFailed= true contributionsCreated= 1'. The repository layer (InMemoryRepositories.ts and SqliteRepositories.ts) exposes no transaction/batch API, so the UI-level Promise.all is the only 'atomicity' mechanism. todo-completion.test.ts lines 226-230 comment claims 'both succeed or both fail' but the test never injects a failure.
findings.requiredFix: Execute the completion as a single atomic operation: add a repository-level transaction (e.g. SQLite withTransactionAsync wrapping the todo update + contribution insert, with an in-memory equivalent) or a completion use-case in the domain/application layer that writes both the todo status and the ContributionEntry in one transaction, and have the UI call that single operation. Add tests that verify failure atomicity: (a) when the todo update fails, no ContributionEntry is created; (b) when the contribution creation fails, the todo is not marked completed; (c) a retry after any failure cannot produce a second ContributionEntry.
findings.verification: New failure-injection tests against the transactional completion path: force the todo update to reject and assert contribRepo.getByHousehold returns 0 entries; force the contribution create to reject and assert the todo status remains 'todo'; then complete successfully and assert exactly 1 ContributionEntry exists. The existing success-path test must be updated to use the atomic operation instead of Promise.all.

findings.problem: Non-blocking — the todo list reads the FULL todo collection (including all completed todos) via repos.todos.getByHousehold and filters in JS, so opening À faire costs proportional to total todo history (a group with 50k completed todos reads 50k rows). The new cost-gates test 'listing active todos excludes completed ones without a full rescan' actually performs the full read + JS filter, so its name overstates what the implementation does. This pattern is pre-existing (the previous todos.tsx did the same) and is not a regression introduced by this candidate, but it should be hardened before V3-08 cost gates.
findings.evidence: todos.tsx line 118: `setTodos(householdTodos.filter((t) => t.status !== 'completed'))` after `repos.todos.getByHousehold(currentHouseholdId)`; SqliteRepositories.ts line 624: `SELECT * FROM todo_items WHERE householdId = ? ORDER BY createdAt DESC` (no status filter) although idx_todos_status(householdId, status) exists; cost-gates-v3-05.test.ts lines 199-203 fetch all 100 todos then filter.
findings.requiredFix: Recommended (later cycle): add a status-filtered query (e.g. getActiveByHousehold using idx_todos_status) or paginate the todo list so the common action is not proportional to total history.
findings.verification: A test seeding 50k completed todos + a handful of active ones asserts the active-todo read touches only the active rows (bounded), not the full collection.

findings.problem: Non-blocking — the reminder-cancel block on completion is an empty if-body with a comment explaining the notification id is not stored on TodoItem. This is honest (notifications.isAvailable() returns false so it is a no-op today), but when a real notification port is wired in a later cycle, completed todos would leave orphan scheduled reminders.
findings.evidence: todos.tsx lines 256-260: `if (selectedTodo.reminderAt && services.notifications.isAvailable()) { // Note: we don't have the notification id stored; this is a best-effort cancel. }`; LocalNotificationAdapter.isAvailable() returns false.
findings.requiredFix: Recommended (later cycle, when a real notification port exists): persist the scheduled notification id on TodoItem (e.g. reminderNotificationId) at creation and cancel it on completion/deletion.
findings.verification: With a fake notification port returning a real id, completing a todo cancels the scheduled notification (cancelNotification called with the stored id).

findings.problem: Non-blocking — the completion value field starts empty instead of prefilling the PersistentTask defaultValue when the todo references one. The constitution allows the default to come from the PersistentTask ('La valeur par défaut peut provenir de la PersistentTask') and the user must confirm the value anyway, so this is a UX convenience gap, not an acceptance failure.
findings.evidence: todos.tsx line 211: `value: '', // User must confirm`; the PersistentTask entity carries defaultValue (entities/index.ts line 71) and the todo carries persistentTaskId, but startComplete never looks up the task's defaultValue.
findings.requiredFix: Recommended: prefill completeForm.value from the referenced PersistentTask's defaultValue (falling back to empty) so the user confirms rather than retypes.
findings.verification: Completing a todo created from a PersistentTask with defaultValue=30 shows 30 in the value field; the user can still edit it before confirming.
